approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted high-scoring molecules using connected-fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. It retains a direct aromatic nitrogen positional exchange and checks stable canonical identities before admitting fresh candidates. A greedy survivor population supplies breeding parents, while all accepted observations train a fingerprint Gaussian process. The process builds a surplus pool and chooses evaluations through correlated posterior draws. Its molecular fingerprints record whether each local environment occurs, discarding how many times it occurs.
approach.novelty: Preserve local-environment multiplicity in that same posterior: use Morgan occurrence counts with count Tanimoto covariance. Repeated aromatic, carbonyl and other environments will then contribute their counts to molecular similarity instead of a single presence flag. This tests whether occurrence weighting improves prediction on the Parent's actual repeat-rich molecules. Earlier siblings changed parent allocation, molecular edits or identity admission; this changes the representation used to transfer accepted scores across their unchanged candidate pools. It does not assume that larger molecules are better or that the existing exact fingerprint ties will separate.

hypothesis: Preserve local-environment multiplicity in the inherited Gaussian-process posterior by replacing binary Morgan features with radius-two 2048-bin Morgan occurrence counts and their dot-product Tanimoto covariance.

finding_summary.headline: Occurrence counts improved prediction and mean best score, while uncertainty coverage deteriorated.
finding_summary.insights:
Multiplicity carries useful information for this accepted-data regime, but stronger similarity also produces narrower uncertainty. On the Child’s fixed pools, mean off-diagonal similarity rose from 0.3267 to 0.5873, and marginal standard deviation fell for 67,687 of 69,600 candidates. Exact feature ties remained inseparable: the Child’s single tied pair and all ten historical Parent ties survive count encoding. This locates the observed effect in changed weighting among distinct fingerprints.

Predictive utility and endpoint utility diverge most clearly on sitagliptin_mpo: it supplies the largest mean score gain, yet count MSE worsened in all three seeds and pooled 1.96-standard-deviation coverage fell from 54.48% to 33.33%. Together with the one regressing seed, this supports investigating uncertainty and task-local transfer separately from the useful covariance change. The matched comparisons establish effects on the actual selected stream; they do not establish an alternative whole-search score or outcomes for unselected molecules.

The supplied chemical assessment still finds repeat-rich ring systems, unconventional heteroatom bonds, unassigned stereochemistry and uneven molecular growth. Count weighting has therefore not demonstrated a remedy for chemical realism, exact fingerprint equivalence or stereochemical coverage. The numerical failure branches also remain untested because no eligible failure occurred.
finding_summary.results:
Occurrence weighting changed every one of the 435 fitted pool distributions across all five tasks and three seeds. On identical accepted data, 69,570 of 69,600 pool means and marginal standard deviations differed from the binary comparator. The logged count predictions, feedback updates and correlated selections reconstructed without mismatch. Reusing the same normal draws with the binary comparator changed 2,768 of 4,350 choice positions in 434 pools; those alternative choices were not scored.

On the 4,350 molecules actually evaluated, count-posterior MSE was 0.011269 versus 0.011797 for the matched binary posterior and 0.042504 for the archive-mean baseline. Mean within-batch rank correlation rose from 0.4694 to 0.5498. Coverage deteriorated: 60.90% versus 71.36% within one latent standard deviation, and 76.92% versus 85.63% within 1.96. All 4,200 eligible next-fit probes changed; standardized uncertainty fell on every probe, while score-unit uncertainty rose on 20 because the archive scale changed. All training and pool factorizations succeeded at the first jitter in both panels.

Recorded final-best macro score rose from 0.551771 to 0.574344, a paired mean gain of 0.022573 against the declared 0.002 criterion. Child and Parent population standard deviations across seeds were 0.012317 and 0.008223; paired-delta standard deviation was 0.020520. Seed gains were +0.044871, -0.004661 and +0.027509. Mean task changes were +0.062135 for sitagliptin_mpo, +0.023333 for median_2, +0.020559 for drd2_docking, +0.009115 for deco_hop and -0.002276 for zaleplon_mpo. Ten of fifteen task-seed endpoints improved. Strict improvements over each offspring’s best generating parent rose from 593 to 624 out of 4,350. These search outcomes include the ensuing changes in generation and feedback.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich scaffold families retain amides and amines, but unusual heteroatom bonds, unassigned stereochemistry and uneven growth persist.
molecular.overall_character: Read the complete child and parent panels: every supplied task at seeds 0, 1 and 2, including all 300 trajectory records per seed. Each child task contains 870 optimizer proposals; all parse in the supplied RDKit environment. This is graph validity, not evidence of a synthetic route or useful biological activity. Passive descriptor and feature counts are derived directly from those SMILES and recorded in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-05-improve-L01.molecular-audit.json. These are predominantly branched, multi-ring molecules with abundant aromatic atoms, carbonyls, ethers, nitrogen heterocycles and halogens. Digest ring-closure hit rates range from 0.9575 to 0.9851 and aromatic-text hit rates from 0.9517 to 0.9747; these are fractions of proposal strings with a feature, not atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Ring topology is genuinely varied across the panel, but the higher-scoring portions of individual seed trajectories repeatedly elaborate a few scaffold families. Some families occupy a conventional medicinal-chemistry size range; another includes very large, repetitive heteroaromatic assemblies. Ordinary amides and basic amine centres are present, so neither rings nor basic nitrogen is globally missing. The main chemistry deficiencies are unreliable preservation of conventional heteroatom bonding, absent stereochemical specification despite newly created stereocentres, limited alternative scaffold coverage around successful motifs, and uncontrolled growth or collapse to tiny fragments. Every task has charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0; neutral SMILES do not imply that its amines cannot protonate. Parent comparisons below describe recorded chemistry and scores only, without attributing changes to algorithm activation. The excerpts of best molecules and final molecules are pooled across seeds; they are not three independent endpoint summaries.

per_task.generated_character: Seeds 1 and 2 mainly produce methyl-, methoxy- and vinyl-substituted indole carboxamides attached to phenyl or pyridyl rings. Seed 0 also reaches a compact bridged nitrogen-containing framework bearing an aryl carboxamide and an N-S substituent. The seed winners have 24, 25 and 24 heavy atoms respectively. Thus this is compact aromatic scaffold elaboration, not a search confined to fragments or lacking ring nitrogen. The ordinary aryl amides look synthetically approachable in principle; the highest-scoring N-S and N-halogen congeners are less conventional. Digest ring/aromatic hit rates are 0.9644/0.9621.
liabilities: N-fluoro and N-chloro amides, plus the terminal N-S attachment in the maximum, raise chemical stability and preparation questions that SMILES sanitization does not answer.
Vinyl ethers, multiple vinyl substituents and complicated bridging add potential reactivity or synthetic burden; late single-heavy-atom proposals also lose essentially all useful molecular context.
missing_features: A consistently conventional realization of the top-scoring aromatic/carboxamide envelope is not demonstrated: ordinary amides occur, but the seed maxima use N-S or N-halogen substitution. The data do not establish that any absent named pharmacophore is required.
The new stereocentre perceived in the seed-0 best graph is unspecified; comparable stereodefined alternatives are absent from the supplied proposals, and their score value is untested.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole fluorophenyl amide scores 0.3051048083696145; the ordinary divinyl, methoxy, pyridyl amide in the digest reaches 0.4330127018922193. Its N-chloro and N-fluoro versions both score 0.4423126980074005, showing that the recorded score does not distinguish those two substitutions here. The seed-0 bridged N-S compound reaches 0.45766047024715. Tiny outputs such as C and F score 0.0, while the final carbonyl-linker-expanded amide scores 0.3057223329855419. The observed gradient favours a specific compact aromatic/carboxamide arrangement over loss of that context, without a general reward for larger size or any evidence that chemical stability improved. Recorded parent-to-child best scores, in seed order, are 0.442313 to 0.457660, 0.460926 to 0.442313, and 0.451975 to 0.448414. Parent and child remain in closely related aromatic amide or carbonyl families, with the child seed-0 maximum using a different bridged N-S structure.

per_task.generated_character: The seed panel contains distinct size regimes. Seed 0 grows repeated azaaromatic, carbonyl-containing and imine-bearing assemblies; seed 1 concentrates on an azaheteroaromatic carbonyl/O-ring core with heteroaryl ether, nitrile and heavily halogenated polyene substituents. Seed 2 instead retains a more compact benzo-fused nitrogen ring, alkoxy groups and an alkoxy-bearing aminomethyl connection to a fluorinated pyridyl ring. Median proposal heavy-atom counts are 91, 46 and 31, compared with parent medians 79, 83 and 39. Growth therefore changes in different directions across seeds. Digest mean SMILES length is 94.6, maximum 266, with ring/aromatic hit rates both 0.9713. Conventional aromatic ethers and azaheterocycles coexist with crowded unsaturated appendages and unusual oxygen connectivity.
liabilities: Very large repeated aromatic assemblies and highly substituted polyenes create substantial synthetic and conformational burdens without a demonstrated reward for each extra fragment.
Halogenated alkenes lack geometric specification; seed-0 cumulated double bonds and the seed-2 O-O/O-halogen variants add chemical liabilities beyond the conventional heterocyclic cores.
missing_features: The leading seed-1 series lacks well-covered compact, ordinary substituent alternatives that preserve its useful heteroaromatic attachment context without repeated halogenated polyene growth; the smaller seed-2 family shows that extreme bulk is not universal to the higher scores.

Consistent preservation of ordinary ether connectivity is missing in part of the proposal stream: passive reading finds O-O bonds in 162 of 290 seed-2 proposals, compared with only 4 in its upper recorded-score quartile and 48 in its lower quartile. These quartiles contain 73 rows each; this is association, not an isolated peroxide effect.
The alkoxy-bearing carbon stereocentre in the compact seed-2 family is not assigned. No additional objective-required motif can be inferred from the visible score gradient alone.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Small molecules such as C#CCl and ClCCl remain at the observed 0.5 floor; the initial cyclic dicarbonyl scaffold scores 0.548381482770623. The digest seed-1 leader and its much more heavily extended brominated/chlorinated polyene congener both score exactly 0.6199818405862896, although their passive molecular weights are 624.431 and 868.744. These examples show tolerance of added bulk, not a demonstrated score benefit from that addition. Seed 2 has a substantially smaller final nitrogen-ring/aryl-ether compound at 0.6109149100540779, whereas the truncated diaryl hydrazine scores 0.5557275541795665. The apparent reward is for retaining favourable heteroaromatic connectivity and substitution context; sheer size is not consistently needed. Parent-to-child seed best scores are 0.609808 to 0.609280, 0.611413 to 0.619982, and 0.597688 to 0.616992. The first pair retains oversized heteroaromatic chemistry, while the latter pairs accompany smaller scaffold families than their parents.

per_task.generated_character: The better molecules combine substituted aromatic surfaces with non-amide aliphatic amines. Seed 1 has N-propyl pyrrolidine attached to compact bridged ether/aryl or azaaryl systems; seed 2 uses saturated nitrogen rings linked to fluorinated biaryl and oxygen-containing rings. Seed 0 keeps a flexible tertiary amine between halogenated aryl regions and reaches unusual sulfur chemistry, including sulfur double-bonded to both carbon and oxygen. Seed winners contain 30, 26 and 31 heavy atoms. Digest ring/aromatic hit rates are 0.9736/0.9655 and halogen hit rate is 0.9885. Basic amine centres and nonplanar saturated rings are clearly present; their exact ionization and configurations are not supplied. Some ring-amine/aryl combinations are medicinally recognizable, while the bridged structures and sulfur endpoints need much stronger synthetic justification.
liabilities: The carbon=sulfur=oxygen motif, extensive halogenation and some N-S/O-halogen edits are unconventional for routine medicinal chemistry; their high recorded scores do not establish stability or accessibility.
Crowded bridged rings and the peroxide-containing final example add stereochemical, conformational and synthetic uncertainty that graph validity does not settle.
missing_features: Stereodefined versions of the favourable ring-amine/aryl geometries are absent: the overall best graph has three perceived but unassigned tetrahedral centres. The supplied scores do not resolve which configurations or protonation states were responsible.

The seed-0 maximum does not demonstrate an ordinary, stable sulfur-linkage realization of its favourable amine/aryl context. Other seeds already show that basic nitrogen on rings can be generated, so a global lack of ring amines would be an incorrect diagnosis.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The compact pyrrolidine/bridged-ether leader scores 0.9964552366323939; the acyclic tertiary-amine, sulfur-rich leader scores 0.9959491085611949. In contrast, the sulfonylated pyrrolidine ketone scores 0.00021169315013374197 and simple aryl sulfonyl derivatives score 0.00024675866379847753. This associates a suitable amine/aryl arrangement with higher scores, but does not prove that an amine alone is sufficient: the initial amine-bearing hydroxamate is also low at 0.0003786988088202195. Upper versus lower score-quartile median heavy-atom counts are 31 versus 41, 30 versus 39, and 31 versus 39 across seeds, so these trajectories do not support a blanket size reward. A final peroxide-containing, heavily bridged seed-2 molecule scores 0.6566255585773542 despite retaining amines. Parent-to-child best scores are 0.979377 to 0.995949, 0.951235 to 0.996455, and 0.991404 to 0.991289. The similar third endpoint accompanies a changed nitrogen-ring/aryl topology; none of these numbers establishes experimental binding or a particular pose.

per_task.generated_character: These are mixed aromatic/aliphatic nitrogen polycycles with recurring N-methyl cyclic amide or dicarbonyl fragments, propyl substituents and aryl groups. Seed 0 forms more densely connected nitrogen/carbonyl rings, seed 1 joins two aryl regions through ether-containing and nitrogen/carbonyl rings, and seed 2 joins a quinoline region to an unsaturated nitrogen-ring/dicarbonyl system. The seed winners have 37, 33 and 30 heavy atoms. The overall best is perceived as four rings, including rings of size ten and seven, with two aromatic rings and two carbonyls; it is not a flat aromatic-only molecule. These are plausible bond patterns for specialized synthetic targets, but ring closure and stereochemical control are substantial unresolved requirements. Digest ring/aromatic hit rates are 0.9851/0.9747 and halogen hit rate is only 0.1356.
liabilities: Medium-sized ring closures, linked ring junctions and N-N connectivity in leading structures complicate route design even when the individual amide and ether groups are familiar.
Some late variants introduce N-S, N-O or O-O connectivity; a dense ring system alone does not make those edits chemically equivalent to the more conventional neighbours.
missing_features: Alternative, less synthetically demanding connections of the favourable aromatic and nitrogen/dicarbonyl fragments are not well represented at the maximum: the pooled best excerpt is concentrated in close variants of the seed-1 family. This is limited chemical coverage, not proof that any particular unseen scaffold would score better.
Defined configurations for the new saturated ring junctions and substituent-bearing centres are absent. The overall leader has an unassigned tetrahedral centre, and the seed-2 endpoint has two.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aromatic cyclic-dicarbonyl example scores 0.1678386594791329, while the connected diaryl-ether/nitrogen-dicarbonyl leader reaches 0.24321515648721753. A different connection of the same formula in the digest scores 0.23979854715495866; retaining component types does not make topology irrelevant. The seed-2 final quinoline/dicarbonyl molecule scores 0.23035161967494103, compared with 0.21717071756426068 for more decorated neighbours and 0.21094823834331713 for the sulfur-containing neighbour. Tiny C, C#C and OO proposals score 0.0. The observed high-score envelope therefore retains both aromatic regions and nitrogen/carbonyl connectivity rather than favouring isolated fragments; it does not imply that adding rings or decorations indefinitely is useful. Parent-to-child seed best scores are 0.204784 to 0.222706, 0.213610 to 0.243215, and 0.207878 to 0.230352. Both panels retain nitrogen/dicarbonyl scaffolds, while the child changes their connections and saturated ring geometry.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 0 supplies the whole pooled best excerpt: anisyl or related aryl groups attached to a fused nitrogen-rich carbonyl/imino heterocycle, with fluorinated small nitrogen rings and frequent N-F attachments. The overall leader has 27 heavy atoms, a carbonyl and an exocyclic imino group, and includes a four-membered unsaturated nitrogen ring. Seed 1 instead develops phenolic aryl/dicarbonyl heterocycles with fluorinated unsaturated side chains; seed 2 develops more compact phenolic aryl/carbonyl-imino analogues with fluoroalkyl substitution. These are medium-sized, aromatic and heteroatom-rich rather than large repeated assemblies. Ring/aromatic hit rates are 0.9575/0.9517 and halogen hit rate is 0.8954. Passive inspection finds N-halogen bonds in 254, 155 and 125 of the 290 proposals in the respective seeds; fluorination is often directly on nitrogen, not solely on carbon.
liabilities: Repeated N-fluorination is a major distinction from ordinary carbon fluorination and raises questions of reactivity and synthetic handling. Passing SMILES perception is insufficient to establish medicinal suitability.
The four-membered unsaturated nitrogen ring, nearby imino functionality and unspecified stereochemistry make the overall leader a more demanding chemical target than its moderate size suggests.
Late emissions still include very small species such as OBr, showing loss of the useful molecular context even after complex higher-scoring structures have been found.
missing_features: The maximum is not demonstrated using a fully conventional set of carbon-bound fluorine and ordinary nitrogen substituents: leading analogues repeatedly retain N-F. It remains unknown whether more ordinary bonding could preserve the observed compact fluorinated carbonyl/imino pattern at comparable scores.

The small-ring substitution creates an unassigned stereocentre in the overall leader. Stereodefined alternatives and a demonstrated less strained realization of the same spatial arrangement are missing; their score benefit cannot be inferred.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl cyclic-dicarbonyl scaffold scores 0.0020944534688323298. Compact fluorinated carbonyl/imino analogues reach 0.6510211907030741 and 0.6492585029324071 in seed 0. Neither fragmentation nor repetition helps these particular examples: F scores 1.1043196211273875e-26 and the duplicated, heavily linked heterocycle in the worst excerpt scores 5.038398954372863e-25. A final seed-2 phenolic aryl analogue scores 0.5136226132583438, whereas a different final compound with an unsaturated aliphatic ring replacing the aryl region scores 0.056329114721316687. This supports a compact fluorinated aryl/heterocycle envelope in the observed stream, without identifying which objective components or individual substitutions cause the reward. Parent-to-child best scores are 0.475978 to 0.651021, 0.575091 to 0.487006, and 0.503080 to 0.602525. The child shifts seed 0 toward the fused imino/N-F family, loses score in the distinct seed-1 family, and simplifies the highly fused parent seed-2 chemistry. The seed-0 excerpt must not be read as a uniform result across seeds.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The digest includes aryl amides bearing N-F or N-Cl, nitrogen-rich carbonyl/imino rings repeatedly bearing N-F, a high-scoring sulfur centre double-bonded to carbon and oxygen, and peroxide-containing ring systems. Passive full-trajectory inspection also finds 162 O-O-containing proposals in one 290-proposal stream, with fewer of those in its upper score quartile. These are observed bond patterns, not inferred synthetic failures.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional functional-group bonding while it modifies otherwise useful molecular frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically ordinary linkage alternatives and preserve functional-group context during edits, so accepted feedback can compare such alternatives with unusual bond arrangements. Valence checking alone cannot supply this capability, and an unusual motif should not be assumed beneficial or worthless merely because it is unusual.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Every task digest reports stereocentre_rate 0.0. Passive parsing confirms unassigned tetrahedral centres in compact bridged amine/aryl leaders, medium-ring carbonyl systems and fluorinated small rings; the bridged amine leader at 0.9964552366323939 has three. No optimizer trajectory uses alkene stereobond markers either.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator creates stereogenic graphs but does not emit defined stereochemical alternatives.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent and explore valid configurations when graph edits create stereogenic atoms or geometrically distinguishable double bonds. The missing capability is configuration coverage; these trajectories do not establish a universal score benefit from adding stereochemistry.

transferable_gaps.evidence: One proposal stream has a median of 91 heavy atoms versus 79 in its parent, while another contracts substantially. The cited halogenated heteroaromatic leader and an extended polyene congener have molecular weights 624.431 and 868.744 but share score 0.6199818405862896. Other high-scoring streams favour smaller molecules than their own lower-scoring groups. Thus growth is chemically uneven and its benefit cannot be assumed.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful scaffold retention is not coupled to reliable exploration of compact alternatives to repeated fragment growth.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose contractions and compact replacements that preserve successful attachment context alongside growth proposals, allowing the local accepted scores to reveal where size or repeated environments matter. A universal growth preference or universal size penalty is not supported by this panel.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Higher-scoring excerpts repeatedly elaborate substituted indole carboxamides, a narrow fused carbonyl/imino heterocycle family, or one connected diaryl/nitrogen-dicarbonyl family. Different seeds do discover different topologies, and topology variants sometimes differ in score, so this is limited local coverage rather than absence of ring-building capability.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-rich output does not provide broad alternative scaffold coverage around each locally successful chemical motif.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make chemically comparable reconnections and scaffold replacements available while retaining the useful aryl, amine or carbonyl context learned from accepted molecules. Seek broader connectivity coverage without embedding a named objective or a presumed target scaffold.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Digest worst and final examples include single-heavy-atom C and F, tiny C#C and OO, and terminal OBr. They lie at or near the bottom of their own recorded score spans even though the same streams already contain complex higher-scoring ring systems.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator still loses nearly all molecular context in a minority of late proposals.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support context-preserving repair or resampling of destructive edits, informed by the accepted molecular history. The observed gap concerns loss of useful structure, not a benchmark-specific minimum size or a claim that all small molecules are undesirable.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

retained_mechanisms: Task-local scored molecular-graph population with score-ranked parent sampling across three high-ranked quantiles.
Local atom and bond mutation with inner operator retries and occasional multi-step graph walks.
Chemical sanitization, canonical/isomeric identity rejection, and graph retries for complete novel pools; bounded saturation branches remain present.
Greedy score-ranked survivor selection and later breeding from accepted offspring.

Accepted-only task-local Gaussian-process archive, exact joint posterior draws over fresh surplus offspring pools, masked correlated batch maximization and feedback-driven posterior refitting; bounded numerical fallback remains present but was not exercised.
Pool-only stable canonical identity admission with graph-equivalent alias normalization retaining the checked molecule and bounded rejection of unresolved representations.

Direct same-six-member-aromatic-ring C/N positional exchange in the inherited per-site replacement menu, with formula/count/aromaticity gates, ordinary checking, novelty admission and passive mutation receipts.

Multiplicity-preserving radius-two 2048-bin Morgan occurrence counts and a shared dot-product count Tanimoto covariance for all training, pool and feedback queries, with unchanged normalization/noise settings and passive ordered feature/timing receipts.

activation_observables.measurement: Reconstruct each Child fit from exactly its ordered earlier accepted training records and pool identities under the installed Morgan generator. Verify integer counts, unchanged binary support, occurrence totals and squared norms; distinguish repeated unfolded sparse environment identifiers from collisions introduced by 2048-bin folding. On identical Child accepted archives, normalization and ordered pools, reconstruct both the declared count posterior and the unchanged Parent binary posterior. Report train/train, train/pool and pool/pool kernel displacement, mean and marginal-SD displacement in score units, and full conditional-covariance displacement in standardized units, using 1e-10 as numerical equality tolerance. Require eligible repeated-count inputs to reach an actually used count kernel and at least one nontrivial posterior mean or covariance difference. Do not call nonconstant counts alone a downstream posterior effect. Reproduce the passive historical Parent counts and source-pair comparisons independently; those comparisons contain no Child prediction or unselected oracle outcome.
activation_observables.name: Reconstruct each fit from its ordered accepted training records and declared feature/kernel/normalization/noise settings; report changed representations, similarity relationships or posterior values only on eligible fixed-data comparisons.

activation_observables.measurement: Join each emitted prediction to the next fit on that identical molecule, checking accepted-only archive membership and excluding the terminal batch when no next suggestion exists. Reconstruct before/after count-posterior means and latent SDs, recording changes in archive mean and scale separately from standardized conditional uncertainty. Also reconstruct the binary comparator on each identical before/after accepted state to isolate the representation-dependent update. Report opportunities, changed probes and displacement distributions; do not equate a lower post-feedback SD with improved calibration or claim the Child update should always be smaller than the Parent's.
activation_observables.name: Compare pre-feedback predictions with the next fit on the identical emitted molecules, excluding terminal observations with no next suggestion; separate changes in normalization from changes in conditional uncertainty.

activation_observables.measurement: On accepted emitted molecules only, join real scores to predictions made before that feedback. Report chronological MSE against the same-fit archive-mean baseline, within-batch rank association, signed residuals and one/1.96 latent-SD coverage by task and supplied seed. Reconstruct the unchanged binary Parent posterior using exactly the Child's contemporaneous accepted data, and compare its prospective errors with the count posterior on those same emitted molecules. Improved MSE or ranking would support predictive utility; coverage must be measured independently and may worsen. The recorded Parent benchmark is MSE 0.016972173172054354 versus archive-mean MSE 0.03606287331064628 with 0.7873563218390804 coverage at 1.96 logged latent SD. Separate same-state prediction comparisons from different-search-trajectory comparisons. Report the complete supplied paired final-best macro/task results and strict parent beats as downstream outcomes, using the supplied 0.002 score criterion; neither passive comparator supplies alternative oracle labels or an alternate whole-search score.
activation_observables.name: Report chronological prediction MSE against the same-fit archive-mean baseline, within-batch rank association and uncertainty coverage on scored emitted molecules, by task and seed; never infer calibration from posterior arithmetic alone.

applicability_conditions: The active fingerprint_posterior Layer permits a representation/covariance change while all other Layer interfaces remain frozen. The authoritative brief supplies the formal panel and resources; the optimizer uses only its announced objective-local accepted observations, with no task identity, corpus, future or unselected labels.

Occurrence counts describe local radius-two environment multiplicity, with the same chirality setting and 2048-bin folding as the Parent. They neither remove hashing nor distinguish molecules with equal count vectors, recover longer-range connectivity, repair unusual chemistry or create missing stereoisomers.

Observed count-sensitive source similarities frequently increase. The mechanism therefore is not a size penalty or an assumed uncertainty increase: repeated common environments may dominate covariance, oversmooth distinct molecules and worsen the already heterogeneous selected-stream coverage. Its score value depends on whether accepted labels support transfer through those counts.

Repeated environments are common in the actual Parent pool, but the source-only structural comparisons do not establish count-posterior predictive superiority. Exact pool fingerprint collisions are rare and all ten observed ties survive the proposed representation; benefit must arise from changed similarity weighting elsewhere.

The inspected Curate history contains no earlier Morgan occurrence-count Gaussian-process change. The retained posterior-sampling cluster concerns allocation through joint draws, which is preserved here; the separate count-descriptor construction cluster concerns added endpoint-degree descriptors in a ridge-guided integer graph program. Neither is this covariance mechanism, so no settled cluster is being revisited.

Same-state passive reconstructions isolate statistical differences but do not score unselected alternatives. Final-best changes include downstream breeding and trajectory effects. Numerical, predictive, calibration and endpoint conclusions must remain separate, including task regressions and full supplied seed dispersion. There is no active Round Injection.

approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted high-scoring molecules using connected-fragment crossover and local atom or bond edits. It retains a direct aromatic nitrogen positional exchange and checks stable canonical identities before admitting fresh candidates. A greedy survivor population supplies breeding parents, while all accepted observations train a fingerprint Gaussian process. The process builds a surplus pool and chooses evaluations through correlated posterior draws. Its molecular fingerprints record whether each local environment occurs, discarding how many times it occurs.
approach.novelty: Preserve local-environment multiplicity in that same posterior: use Morgan occurrence counts with count Tanimoto covariance. Repeated aromatic, carbonyl and other environments will then contribute their counts to molecular similarity instead of a single presence flag. This tests whether occurrence weighting improves prediction on the Parent's actual repeat-rich molecules. Earlier siblings changed parent allocation, molecular edits or identity admission; this changes the representation used to transfer accepted scores across their unchanged candidate pools. It does not assume that larger molecules are better or that the existing exact fingerprint ties will separate.

finding_summary.headline: Occurrence counts improved prediction and mean best score, while uncertainty coverage deteriorated.
finding_summary.insights:
Multiplicity carries useful information for this accepted-data regime, but stronger similarity also produces narrower uncertainty. On the Child’s fixed pools, mean off-diagonal similarity rose from 0.3267 to 0.5873, and marginal standard deviation fell for 67,687 of 69,600 candidates. Exact feature ties remained inseparable: the Child’s single tied pair and all ten historical Parent ties survive count encoding. This locates the observed effect in changed weighting among distinct fingerprints.

Predictive utility and endpoint utility diverge most clearly on sitagliptin_mpo: it supplies the largest mean score gain, yet count MSE worsened in all three seeds and pooled 1.96-standard-deviation coverage fell from 54.48% to 33.33%. Together with the one regressing seed, this supports investigating uncertainty and task-local transfer separately from the useful covariance change. The matched comparisons establish effects on the actual selected stream; they do not establish an alternative whole-search score or outcomes for unselected molecules.

The supplied chemical assessment still finds repeat-rich ring systems, unconventional heteroatom bonds, unassigned stereochemistry and uneven molecular growth. Count weighting has therefore not demonstrated a remedy for chemical realism, exact fingerprint equivalence or stereochemical coverage. The numerical failure branches also remain untested because no eligible failure occurred.
finding_summary.results:
Occurrence weighting changed every one of the 435 fitted pool distributions across all five tasks and three seeds. On identical accepted data, 69,570 of 69,600 pool means and marginal standard deviations differed from the binary comparator. The logged count predictions, feedback updates and correlated selections reconstructed without mismatch. Reusing the same normal draws with the binary comparator changed 2,768 of 4,350 choice positions in 434 pools; those alternative choices were not scored.

On the 4,350 molecules actually evaluated, count-posterior MSE was 0.011269 versus 0.011797 for the matched binary posterior and 0.042504 for the archive-mean baseline. Mean within-batch rank correlation rose from 0.4694 to 0.5498. Coverage deteriorated: 60.90% versus 71.36% within one latent standard deviation, and 76.92% versus 85.63% within 1.96. All 4,200 eligible next-fit probes changed; standardized uncertainty fell on every probe, while score-unit uncertainty rose on 20 because the archive scale changed. All training and pool factorizations succeeded at the first jitter in both panels.

Recorded final-best macro score rose from 0.551771 to 0.574344, a paired mean gain of 0.022573 against the declared 0.002 criterion. Child and Parent population standard deviations across seeds were 0.012317 and 0.008223; paired-delta standard deviation was 0.020520. Seed gains were +0.044871, -0.004661 and +0.027509. Mean task changes were +0.062135 for sitagliptin_mpo, +0.023333 for median_2, +0.020559 for drd2_docking, +0.009115 for deco_hop and -0.002276 for zaleplon_mpo. Ten of fifteen task-seed endpoints improved. Strict improvements over each offspring’s best generating parent rose from 593 to 624 out of 4,350. These search outcomes include the ensuing changes in generation and feedback.

finding_summary.headline: Occurrence counts improved prediction and mean best score, while uncertainty coverage deteriorated.
finding_summary.insights:
Multiplicity carries useful information for this accepted-data regime, but stronger similarity also produces narrower uncertainty. On the Child’s fixed pools, mean off-diagonal similarity rose from 0.3267 to 0.5873, and marginal standard deviation fell for 67,687 of 69,600 candidates. Exact feature ties remained inseparable: the Child’s single tied pair and all ten historical Parent ties survive count encoding. This locates the observed effect in changed weighting among distinct fingerprints.

Predictive utility and endpoint utility diverge most clearly on sitagliptin_mpo: it supplies the largest mean score gain, yet count MSE worsened in all three seeds and pooled 1.96-standard-deviation coverage fell from 54.48% to 33.33%. Together with the one regressing seed, this supports investigating uncertainty and task-local transfer separately from the useful covariance change. The matched comparisons establish effects on the actual selected stream; they do not establish an alternative whole-search score or outcomes for unselected molecules.

The supplied chemical assessment still finds repeat-rich ring systems, unconventional heteroatom bonds, unassigned stereochemistry and uneven molecular growth. Count weighting has therefore not demonstrated a remedy for chemical realism, exact fingerprint equivalence or stereochemical coverage. The numerical failure branches also remain untested because no eligible failure occurred.
finding_summary.results:
Occurrence weighting changed every one of the 435 fitted pool distributions across all five tasks and three seeds. On identical accepted data, 69,570 of 69,600 pool means and marginal standard deviations differed from the binary comparator. The logged count predictions, feedback updates and correlated selections reconstructed without mismatch. Reusing the same normal draws with the binary comparator changed 2,768 of 4,350 choice positions in 434 pools; those alternative choices were not scored.

On the 4,350 molecules actually evaluated, count-posterior MSE was 0.011269 versus 0.011797 for the matched binary posterior and 0.042504 for the archive-mean baseline. Mean within-batch rank correlation rose from 0.4694 to 0.5498. Coverage deteriorated: 60.90% versus 71.36% within one latent standard deviation, and 76.92% versus 85.63% within 1.96. All 4,200 eligible next-fit probes changed; standardized uncertainty fell on every probe, while score-unit uncertainty rose on 20 because the archive scale changed. All training and pool factorizations succeeded at the first jitter in both panels.

Recorded final-best macro score rose from 0.551771 to 0.574344, a paired mean gain of 0.022573 against the declared 0.002 criterion. Child and Parent population standard deviations across seeds were 0.012317 and 0.008223; paired-delta standard deviation was 0.020520. Seed gains were +0.044871, -0.004661 and +0.027509. Mean task changes were +0.062135 for sitagliptin_mpo, +0.023333 for median_2, +0.020559 for drd2_docking, +0.009115 for deco_hop and -0.002276 for zaleplon_mpo. Ten of fifteen task-seed endpoints improved. Strict improvements over each offspring’s best generating parent rose from 593 to 624 out of 4,350. These search outcomes include the ensuing changes in generation and feedback.

Multiplicity carries useful information for this accepted-data regime, but stronger similarity also produces narrower uncertainty. On the Child’s fixed pools, mean off-diagonal similarity rose from 0.3267 to 0.5873, and marginal standard deviation fell for 67,687 of 69,600 candidates. Exact feature ties remained inseparable: the Child’s single tied pair and all ten historical Parent ties survive count encoding. This locates the observed effect in changed weighting among distinct fingerprints.

Predictive utility and endpoint utility diverge most clearly on sitagliptin_mpo: it supplies the largest mean score gain, yet count MSE worsened in all three seeds and pooled 1.96-standard-deviation coverage fell from 54.48% to 33.33%. Together with the one regressing seed, this supports investigating uncertainty and task-local transfer separately from the useful covariance change. The matched comparisons establish effects on the actual selected stream; they do not establish an alternative whole-search score or outcomes for unselected molecules.

The supplied chemical assessment still finds repeat-rich ring systems, unconventional heteroatom bonds, unassigned stereochemistry and uneven molecular growth. Count weighting has therefore not demonstrated a remedy for chemical realism, exact fingerprint equivalence or stereochemical coverage. The numerical failure branches also remain untested because no eligible failure occurred.

molecular_assessment.headline: Ring-rich scaffold families retain amides and amines, but unusual heteroatom bonds, unassigned stereochemistry and uneven growth persist.
molecular_assessment.overall_character: Read the complete child and parent panels: every supplied task at seeds 0, 1 and 2, including all 300 trajectory records per seed. Each child task contains 870 optimizer proposals; all parse in the supplied RDKit environment. This is graph validity, not evidence of a synthetic route or useful biological activity. Passive descriptor and feature counts are derived directly from those SMILES and recorded in .slots/SPIRAL2.r0011-05-improve-L01.molecular-audit.json. These are predominantly branched, multi-ring molecules with abundant aromatic atoms, carbonyls, ethers, nitrogen heterocycles and halogens. Digest ring-closure hit rates range from 0.9575 to 0.9851 and aromatic-text hit rates from 0.9517 to 0.9747; these are fractions of proposal strings with a feature, not atom fractions or perceived ring counts. Ring topology is genuinely varied across the panel, but the higher-scoring portions of individual seed trajectories repeatedly elaborate a few scaffold families. Some families occupy a conventional medicinal-chemistry size range; another includes very large, repetitive heteroaromatic assemblies. Ordinary amides and basic amine centres are present, so neither rings nor basic nitrogen is globally missing. The main chemistry deficiencies are unreliable preservation of conventional heteroatom bonding, absent stereochemical specification despite newly created stereocentres, limited alternative scaffold coverage around successful motifs, and uncontrolled growth or collapse to tiny fragments. Every task has charged_rate 0.0 and stereocentre_rate 0.0; neutral SMILES do not imply that its amines cannot protonate. Parent comparisons below describe recorded chemistry and scores only, without attributing changes to algorithm activation. The excerpts of best molecules and final molecules are pooled across seeds; they are not three independent endpoint summaries.

per_task.generated_character: Seeds 1 and 2 mainly produce methyl-, methoxy- and vinyl-substituted indole carboxamides attached to phenyl or pyridyl rings. Seed 0 also reaches a compact bridged nitrogen-containing framework bearing an aryl carboxamide and an N-S substituent. The seed winners have 24, 25 and 24 heavy atoms respectively. Thus this is compact aromatic scaffold elaboration, not a search confined to fragments or lacking ring nitrogen. The ordinary aryl amides look synthetically approachable in principle; the highest-scoring N-S and N-halogen congeners are less conventional. Digest ring/aromatic hit rates are 0.9644/0.9621.
liabilities: N-fluoro and N-chloro amides, plus the terminal N-S attachment in the maximum, raise chemical stability and preparation questions that SMILES sanitization does not answer.
Vinyl ethers, multiple vinyl substituents and complicated bridging add potential reactivity or synthetic burden; late single-heavy-atom proposals also lose essentially all useful molecular context.
missing_features: A consistently conventional realization of the top-scoring aromatic/carboxamide envelope is not demonstrated: ordinary amides occur, but the seed maxima use N-S or N-halogen substitution. The data do not establish that any absent named pharmacophore is required.
The new stereocentre perceived in the seed-0 best graph is unspecified; comparable stereodefined alternatives are absent from the supplied proposals, and their score value is untested.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial trimethoxy indole fluorophenyl amide scores 0.3051048083696145; the ordinary divinyl, methoxy, pyridyl amide in the digest reaches 0.4330127018922193. Its N-chloro and N-fluoro versions both score 0.4423126980074005, showing that the recorded score does not distinguish those two substitutions here.
